description: Remove project and repository local paths, configure repositories by Git URL, and run all workflow work inside runner-managed isolated workspaces.

tasks.title: Make projects pathless
tasks.description: Remove project local checkout concepts from the backend project model and lifecycle. Project creation must create only a Mohist scope and must not inspect filesystem paths, infer Git branches, or create repositories from local directories.
acceptanceCriteria: Project domain, persistence rows, API DTOs, and read models omit path, effectivePath, checkout path, and project-level baseBranch fields.
POST /api/projects accepts a name-only body and returns a project without local checkout fields.
Project creation executes no Git commands and does not create a default repository from a project path.
Project list/use/delete behavior remains functional without path data.
Backend tests cover name-only create, list responses without paths, and no default repository derived from a path.
tasks.output: Pathless project domain/API behavior and tests
tasks.notes: No legacy migration or compatibility shim is required.

tasks.title: Require repository Git URLs
tasks.description: Replace repository path/remote/resolvedPath contracts with Git source metadata. Repository create and update operations must require gitUrl and persist only name, gitUrl, baseBranch, and isDefault.
acceptanceCriteria: Repository domain, persistence rows, API DTOs, read models, and UI-facing data omit path, remote, resolvedPath, and local checkout equivalents.
Repository create/update accepts name, gitUrl, baseBranch, and isDefault and returns those fields.
Repository create/update with path and no gitUrl fails with a 400-class validation error and does not mutate state.
Default repository selection is based only on explicit repository metadata containing gitUrl and baseBranch.
Backend tests cover successful Git URL repository configuration and path-only rejection.
tasks.output: Git URL repository model/API behavior and tests
tasks.notes: Use public field name gitUrl everywhere instead of keeping internal Remote terminology.

tasks.title: Prepare isolated workflow workspaces
tasks.description: Replace git-worktree-based preparation with runner-owned repository cache and isolated workflow workspace creation under MOHIST_RUNNER_ROOT. The runner must clone or fetch from repository.gitUrl, materialize the configured baseBranch into a separate workspace, and return workspace.path for workflow execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Workspace preparation clones or fetches repository.gitUrl into runner-managed cache state under MOHIST_RUNNER_ROOT.
Each active workflow run reuses or creates a separate workspace directory under MOHIST_RUNNER_ROOT that is not the repository cache.
Preparation checks out or materializes repository.baseBranch in the workspace and fails clearly when the configured branch cannot be resolved from gitUrl.
Runner preparation does not execute git worktree add, git worktree list, git worktree remove, git worktree prune, or derive paths from project local checkout data.
Runner tests cover cache-from-gitUrl, workspace reuse, branch-resolution failure, and absence of git worktree commands.
tasks.output: Runner workspace manager backed by Git URL cache and isolated workspaces
tasks.notes: Cache paths are implementation details and must never become action cwd or public repository fields.

tasks.title: Persist workspace identity on runs
tasks.description: Attach the runner-created workflow workspace identity to WorkflowRun state during issue start and reuse it for resume, inspection, and cleanup. WorkflowRun startup must use repository gitUrl/baseBranch metadata and must not depend on project or repository local paths.
acceptanceCriteria: Starting an eligible issue creates or reuses one active WorkflowRun with a persisted workspace identity and workspace.path.
Idempotent start or resume reuses the existing active run and existing workspace rather than creating a duplicate workspace.
Waiting prerequisites prevent WorkflowRun and workspace creation.
Persisted Project and Repository models remain free of local execution path fields after start and cleanup.
Workflow tests cover active run reuse, workspace persistence, prerequisite blocking, and pathless project/repository persistence.
tasks.output: WorkflowRun start/resume behavior with persisted workspace identity
tasks.notes: Workspace identity is a runtime fact scoped to a run, not project or repository configuration.

tasks.title: Constrain workflow dispatch variables
tasks.description: Update workflow dispatch construction so task, check, repair, merge, and approval work receives repository metadata plus workspace.path only. Remove project.path, project.effectivePath, repository.path, repository.remote, repository.resolvedPath, repository cache paths, and user checkout paths from serialized variables and prompt context.
acceptanceCriteria: Dispatch variables include repository.gitUrl, repository.baseBranch, and workspace.path for workflow work items.
Dispatch variables do not include project path, project effectivePath, repository path, repository remote, repository resolvedPath, repository cache path, or user checkout path fields.
Built-in workflow templates and prompts cannot select removed path variables as work directories.
Issue start APIs expose repository Git URL metadata and workspace status without local repository path fields.
Tests assert serialized dispatch variables contain workspace.path and omit all removed path fields.
tasks.output: Workspace-only dispatch variable contract and tests
tasks.notes: This is the data-contract enforcement point for workflow templates and runner actions.

tasks.title: Enforce action cwd isolation
tasks.description: Ensure ACP agent tasks, named session reuse, scripts, checks, OpenSpec sync/archive, rebase, repair, merge, and conflict-resolution actions all execute with context.workDir equal to workspace.path. Remove any action cwd override that switches to project paths, repository cache paths, or external checkouts.
acceptanceCriteria: ACP-backed task sessions start and continue in the workflow workspace cwd.
Named session reuse preserves the original workflow workspace boundary for subsequent prompts.
Script, check, OpenSpec sync/archive, rebase, repair, merge, and conflict-resolution commands run with cwd equal to context.workDir.
Action configuration cannot opt out of workspace isolation or select repository cache/project/user checkout directories.
Runner tests cover agent cwd, named session reuse cwd, script/check cwd, and negative assertions against external cwd usage.
tasks.output: Runner action execution boundary enforcement and tests
tasks.notes: The runner should treat context.workDir/workspace.path as the single execution directory.

tasks.title: Isolate merge and conflict handling
tasks.description: Update mergeability preflight, authoritative mohist/merge, and conflict resolver flows to operate entirely inside the workflow workspace. Merge failures must return structured diagnostics without mutating external checkouts, repository cache state, or project configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Mergeability preflight runs git merge --squash checks inside the workflow workspace and leaves external refs unchanged.
Authoritative Integrate squash merge runs inside the workflow workspace and reports targetBranch, strategy, conflict files, baseSha, candidateHeadSha, and mergeBaseSha on failure.
Conflict resolver reads and writes only files inside the workflow workspace and inherits the merge/rebase/repair workspace cwd.
Merge and conflict code never uses project.path, repository cache path, or a user checkout directory as cwd.
Tests cover clean preflight, conflicting preflight, final merge race diagnostics, and conflict resolver cwd isolation.
tasks.notes: This task focuses on the issue #82 failure mode and should include regression coverage.

tasks.title: Reshape workspace review APIs
tasks.description: Update diff, commits, commit diff, file-content, status, and cleanup APIs to operate on WorkflowRun workspace identity instead of project path plus mo/issue-N worktree assumptions. Issue-level review data must use merge-base comparison semantics and availability-aware responses.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/issues/:number/diff returns available review data with base, head, mergeBase, ahead, behind, canFastForward, comparison=merge-base, summary, files, and patches computed inside the workspace.
Diff output excludes files changed only on base when the issue branch is behind base.
GET /api/issues/:number/commits returns matching comparison metadata and commits reachable from head and not base.
Unavailable review data returns available=false with reason workspace_removed, not_started, branch_missing, or git_error and a displayable message.
Status, file-content, and cleanup responses use workspace terminology and do not expose worktree paths or mo/issue-N assumptions.
API tests cover merge-base diff, commits metadata, commit-scoped diff, unavailable reasons, and workspace cleanup semantics.
tasks.output: Workspace-based review/status/file/cleanup API behavior and tests
tasks.notes: Route names may remain compatible if needed, but public fields and user-facing messages must use workspace semantics.

tasks.title: Update CLI contracts for pathless projects
tasks.description: Update CLI project and repository commands to match the new API contracts. Project creation submits only a name, project listing omits local paths, and repository commands require Git URL metadata rather than accepting local path-only configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: mohist project create <name> sends POST /api/projects with no path, effectivePath, checkout path, or baseBranch field.
mohist project list displays project names and current marker without local path columns or values.
Repository CLI commands submit gitUrl, baseBranch, name, and isDefault and do not submit path, remote, or resolvedPath.
Path-only repository CLI input is rejected before or by the API with a clear validation error.
CLI tests cover name-only project creation, pathless listing, Git URL repository creation, and path-only rejection.
tasks.output: CLI pathless project and Git URL repository behavior with tests
tasks.notes: Keep CLI output language aligned with workspace terminology where workflow execution data is shown.

tasks.title: Update Web project creation
tasks.description: Update Web project creation surfaces and API client methods so users create Mohist project scopes by name only. Remove filesystem browsing, path validation, recent directory selection, and path submission from the project creation flow.
acceptanceCriteria: CreateProjectDialog asks only for project name and does not show, browse, validate, or submit a local filesystem path.
api.createProject sends POST /api/projects with body { name } and expects a Project without path or effectivePath.
Successful creation switches to the new project and refreshes the project list.
Duplicate-name errors keep the dialog open and display the existing error behavior.
Web tests cover name-only submission, no Path is required validation, no directory browser, and project switch/list refresh.
tasks.output: Web name-only project creation and tests
tasks.notes: Remove obsolete local directory browser behavior for project creation rather than hiding it behind a flag.

tasks.title: Update Web repository settings
tasks.description: Update Settings > Repositories to configure Git sources only. The UI must show and edit name, gitUrl, baseBranch, and isDefault, and must stop presenting Local Path and Remote URL as equivalent repository address choices.
acceptanceCriteria: Repository add/edit forms require Git URL and base branch inputs and do not show a Local Path input.
Repository list rows show name, Git URL, base branch, and default status without local checkout or resolved path values.
Submitted repository requests include gitUrl rather than path or remote.
Validation and error messages refer to Git URL, not local path or remote alias configuration.
Web tests cover add repository submission, local path field removal, repository list display, and path/remote omission.
tasks.output: Web Git URL repository settings and tests
tasks.notes: Use gitUrl consistently in Web types and API client payloads.

tasks.title: Rename worktree UI to workspace
tasks.description: Update Web UI labels, empty states, cleanup confirmations, review surfaces, and API data handling so users see workflow workspace terminology. Remove references that tell users to inspect or remove a git worktree under a project path.
acceptanceCriteria: Issue diff, commits, changed-files, file-content, and unavailable-data UI describe data as workflow workspace data.
Cleanup labels and confirmations refer to cleaning a workflow workspace and do not say git worktree.
UI no longer displays mo/issue-N worktree assumptions or project-path inspection guidance.
Frontend types match workspace-based status/review API fields.
Web tests or snapshots cover workspace wording on review and cleanup surfaces.
tasks.output: Workspace terminology in Web review/status/cleanup surfaces
tasks.notes: Prefer public terminology cleanup over broad internal class renames unless required for correctness.

tasks.title: Remove path contracts end-to-end
tasks.description: Add an end-to-end regression sweep that validates removed path/worktree contracts do not leak through project, repository, issue start, workflow dispatch, runner action, review API, CLI, or Web surfaces. This task should close gaps left by earlier implementation tasks and update documentation notes for the breaking model change.
acceptanceCriteria: End-to-end tests or contract tests assert project.path, project.effectivePath, repository.path, repository.remote, repository.resolvedPath, and repository cache paths are absent from public responses and dispatch variables.
Searchable user-facing strings no longer present Local Path as project/repository configuration or use worktree terminology for workflow execution surfaces.
No workflow execution code path invokes git worktree add, git worktree remove, git worktree list, or git worktree prune.
Documentation or release notes state that projects are pathless and repositories require Git URL/base branch metadata, with no compatibility migration.
Full relevant backend, runner, CLI, and Web test suites pass or any unrelated failures are documented.
tasks.output: End-to-end contract regression coverage and breaking-change documentation
tasks.notes: Use this as the final integration task after all implementation surfaces are updated.
